name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a single low-traffic branch in the main repo. This lets us test its impact without risking disruption to active work. The trade-off is delayed visibility into improvement gains, but safety outweighs speed here. If the dry run succeeds, we scale to more branches.

name: Gauge
text: Dry-run hides the signal: PR-Agent’s misses stay invisible until a real PR fails. A better test is a *shadow run*—let it review real PRs but block nothing, logging errors so we see its actual blind spots without risking broken merges. Settle it by running the shadow mode for two weeks and comparing its logged misses to the team’s own review logs.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the shadow mode on the *oldest* merged PR with known issues to get the fastest signal on catch-rate without waiting two weeks. This cuts the test time from weeks to days while still measuring real-world performance.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR with known issues. This gives us the fastest signal on its catch-rate—days, not weeks—because we’re testing against real, problematic code. The trade-off is accepting zero disruption to active work, since it only logs errors without blocking anything. If it misses critical issues, we’ll know immediately and can adjust before scaling.
